settings.title: The Tabi Journey
settings.subtitle: A journey towards slower, more mindful living.

settings.title: Made to order
settings.text: Much of our clothing is made after an order is placed.

settings.heading:
The things we choose to live with
deserve a little thought
settings.text: Tabi began with a love for natural fabrics, the hands that work with them, and the small pleasures of everyday life. Today, we make clothing for women and children, textiles for the home, and objects meant to become part of the way we live. Each is a different expression of the same belief.

settings.caption: A cup of tea before the house wakes up.
A shirt that feels right the moment you put it on.
Children running through the last hour of sunlight.
The familiar tray you bring out when friends arrive.

settings.heading: The things we return to
settings.text: Some of the nicest parts of a day are easily overlooked.
settings.footer_text: This is the life we design for. It is ordinary, sometimes messy, often beautiful. We want the things we make to belong naturally to it.

settings.heading: A lifetime in textiles
settings.text:
Our roots go back decades, to a family garment-making business and a lifetime spent understanding cloth.

Long before Tabi, there were years of working with fabrics, developing designs, refining fits and making garments for people around the world.

That experience remains part of how we work today.

We know how much difference the right fabric can make. How a few changes to a cut can alter the way something feels. How the smallest finishing details can make a piece worth keeping.

Tabi gives us the freedom to bring that knowledge into collections that feel personally meaningful to us.

settings.label: Natural fabrics
settings.caption: The lightness of cotton cambric. The crisp hand of poplin. The structure of twill. The softness that comes with a well-worn piece of clothing.

settings.label: Block print
settings.caption: We love handwork, too. The tiny variations in a block print.

settings.label: Embroidery
settings.caption: The character of an embroidered flower, the unexpected charm of patchwork.

settings.heading:
Made to be worn.
Made to be lived with.
settings.text: We have a particular affection for natural fabrics.
settings.footer_text: Some of our pieces are quiet and understated. Others have plenty of personality. What matters is that they're enjoyable to use, comfortable to live with, and interesting enough to keep coming back to.

settings.label: Product
settings.caption:
A garment's value isn't determined by how green its label looks.

It's in the fabric you enjoy wearing, the fit you reach for again, the details you continue to appreciate, and the years of use it finds in your wardrobe.

We choose natural fabrics and explore craft and design with that longer relationship in mind.

Because the things we value are often the things we take better care of.

settings.label: Process
settings.caption:
We believe in making closer to demand and being accountable for what remains.

Much of our clothing is made after an order is placed, rather than producing large quantities in anticipation of sales.

We also find new uses for leftover fabrics through patchwork, smaller textile products and other upcycling initiatives.

There is always room to improve how we work. What matters is being willing to examine the process, not just admire the finished product.

settings.label: People
settings.caption:
Behind every garment is someone who knows how to make it.

Someone who understands the fabric, guides it through a sewing machine, finishes a seam, embroiders a flower or makes sure the final piece is ready to wear.

We believe their working environment should reflect the value of that skill.

Natural daylight, clean and hygienic facilities, comfortable space between workstations, and wages that recognise their contribution are all part of how we operate.

These might sound like ordinary expectations. In 2026, they should be.

For us, the people who make Tabi are not simply a part of the production process. They are the people who make everything else possible.

settings.heading:
A little more thought
behind what we make
settings.text: We believe the responsibility of making something extends beyond the finished product. It matters what we make, how we make it, and the lives of the people who make it. At Tabi, we think about this through three connected ideas: Product, Process and People.

settings.heading: Giving fabric another life
settings.text: Making things inevitably leaves things behind. And when you have spent a lifetime working with textiles, it becomes difficult to look at a piece of leftover fabric and see only waste. Through Upcycle by Tabi, we've explored ways of giving fabric remnants a new purpose.
settings.footer_text: Some become patchwork and smaller textile pieces. Others are repurposed as filling for mattresses that find their way to families in our wider community. A piece of fabric may have finished one journey, but that doesn't always mean it has nothing left to give. It's a small but meaningful part of how we continue learning to make more responsibly.

settings.heading: The journey continues
settings.text:
Tabi takes its name from the Japanese word for journey. We began with clothing, but our curiosity has always extended to the way we live. The fabrics we bring into our homes. The objects we reach for every day. The rituals we share with the people around us.

As Tabi grows, so will the ways we explore these ideas. We don't have a finished picture of everything Tabi will become. And perhaps that's what makes the journey interesting.

For now, we're glad you're here.
